exposure: non-metropolitan vs. metropolitan birthing parent residence
outcome: prevalence of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP)
cohort: Pregnant individuals from U.S. Natality data between 2016 and 2018.
finding: The prevalence of chronic hypertension and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy is elevated among birthing parents residing in non-metropolitan areas, and neonates born to these parents in non-metropolitan areas have a higher prevalence of APGAR <7 and stillbirth/neonatal death, even after adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics.
